hook.convey: a list that grows by the same amount each time (score after each over, children getting on a bus) → that same amount is the pattern's rule; the rule finds the next number

use.hi: Cricket match mein ek team ka score har over ke baad 7, 14, 21 run tha. Har over mein utne hi run jude. Aisi list ko pattern kehte hain, aur aaj iska agla number nikalna seekhenge.
use.en: In a cricket match, a team's score after each over was 7, 14, 21 runs. The same number of runs came in every over. A list like this is called a pattern, and today we learn to find its next number.

use.hi: Ek school bus har stop pe 4 aur bachchon ko leti hai, toh bus mein bachche hote hain 6, 10, 14. Har stop pe wahi 4 judte hain, yahi is pattern ka niyam hai.
use.en: A school bus picks up 4 more children at every stop, so the bus has 6, 10, 14 children. The same 4 are added at every stop; that is this pattern's rule.

explain.convey: 4, 7, 10, 13 as hops on a number line: every hop is +3 → rule 'add 3 each time'; the rule carries the pattern forward past the last number

point.hi: Dekho, pattern hai 4, 7, 10, 13. 4 se 7 tak 3 ki chhalaang, 7 se 10 tak bhi 3, aur 10 se 13 tak bhi 3. Har kadam pe wahi 3 judta hai, toh niyam hai: har baar 3 jodo.
point.en: Look, the pattern is 4, 7, 10, 13. From 4 to 7 is a jump of 3, from 7 to 10 is also 3, and from 10 to 13 is also 3. The same 3 is added at every step, so the rule is: add 3 each time.

prompt.hi: Board ka pattern 4, 7, 10, 13 aage badhao. 13 ke baad aane wale do numbers mein se doosra kaunsa hai?
prompt.en: Continue the board's pattern 4, 7, 10, 13. Of the two numbers that come after 13, which is the second one?

explain.convey: 2, 7, 12, 18: the first two steps are +5 but the last is +6 → check every step, not just the first; this list is not 'add 5 each time'

point.hi: Is list 2, 7, 12, 18 mein pehle do kadam 5-5 ke hain, par aakhri kadam 12 se 18 tak 6 ka hai. Isliye har kadam check karo, sirf pehla nahi. Yeh list 'har baar 5 jodo' wala pattern nahi hai.
point.en: In this list 2, 7, 12, 18 the first two steps are 5 each, but the last step, from 12 to 18, is 6. So check every step, not just the first. This list is not an 'add 5 each time' pattern.

prompt.hi: Board ki list 2, 7, 12, 18 ko 'har baar 5 jodo' wala pattern banana hai. Toh 18 ki jagah kaunsa number hona chahiye?
prompt.en: We want to make the board's list 2, 7, 12, 18 into an 'add 5 each time' pattern. Which number should be in place of 18?

problem.hi: Pattern hai 7, 12, 17, 22. Iska agla number kaunsa hai?
problem.en: The pattern is 7, 12, 17, 22. What is its next number?

do.hi: Har kadam ka farak nikalo: 7 se 12, 12 se 17, 17 se 22
do.en: Find the change at each step: 7 to 12, 12 to 17, 17 to 22

why.hi: teeno kadam check kiye, aur teeno 5 ke hain
why.en: all three steps were checked, and all three are 5

do.en: Now say the rule in words

why.hi: har kadam pe wahi 5 judta hai
why.en: the same 5 is added at every step

prompt.hi: Ab yeh niyam aakhri number 22 pe lagao. 22 ke baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: Now use this rule on the last number, 22. Which number comes after 22?

why.hi: har kadam pe 5 judta hai, aur 22 mein 5 jodne se 27 aata hai
why.en: every step adds 5, and 22 plus 5 makes 27

prompt.hi: Do pattern hain. A: 5, 9, 13, 17. B: 5, 9, 14, 20. Kaunsa pattern har baar same number jodta hai: A, B, ya dono?
prompt.en: There are two patterns. A: 5, 9, 13, 17. B: 5, 9, 14, 20. Which pattern adds the same number every time: A, B, or both?

prompt.hi: Pattern 4, 10, 16, 23, 29 mein har kadam check karo. Kaunsa kadam baaki se alag hai: pehla, doosra, teesra, chautha, ya koi nahi?
prompt.en: Check every step in the pattern 4, 10, 16, 23, 29. Which step is different from the others: the first, second, third, fourth, or none?

ladder.why: warm-up: 2, 5, 8, 11 → find the +3 and carry it one step
same rule in money: ₹18, ₹25, ₹32 → +7 checked on both steps, day 4
contrast: two lists start 1, 2 but only one adds the same each time → check every step
harder: rule +50 carried three steps ahead to week 6

remediation.move: difference row under the list: write every step, not just the first → 3, 7, 11, 16 has steps 4, 4, 5 → one step differs, so the rule 'add 4' fails; then a fresh list to check

say.hi: Har do numbers ke beech ka kadam likho, sirf pehla nahi. 3, 7, 11, 16 mein kadam hain 4, 4 aur 5, toh yeh 'har baar 4 jodo' wala pattern nahi.
say.en: Write the step between every two numbers, not just the first. In 3, 7, 11, 16 the steps are 4, 4 and 5, so this is not an 'add 4 each time' pattern.

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 10, 16, 22, 29. Kya iska niyam 'har baar 6 jodo' hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The pattern is 10, 16, 22, 29. Is its rule 'add 6 each time', yes or no?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak ke pattern har baar badhte gaye. Ab aise pattern dekhenge jo ghatte hain, dugne hote hain, ya jinka kadam badalta hai.
bridgeToNext.en: So far our patterns kept going up. Now we will see patterns that go down, double, or change their step.

hook.convey: patterns need not go up: a rocket countdown goes down by a fixed step; game coins that double after each level do not add the same amount, yet follow a rule

use.hi: ISRO ke rocket launch se pehle countdown sunte ho: 10, 9, 8, 7. Yahan numbers ghat rahe hain, phir bhi yeh ek pattern hai.
use.en: Before an ISRO rocket launch you hear the countdown: 10, 9, 8, 7. Here the numbers are going down, and still it is a pattern.

use.hi: Ek video game mein har level up pe coins dugne ho jaate hain: 5, 10, 20, 40. Yahan har baar same number nahi judta, phir bhi iska ek niyam hai.
use.en: In a video game, the coins double at every level up: 5, 10, 20, 40. Here the same number is not added each time, and still it has a rule.

explain.convey: 38, 32, 26, 20 as backward hops of 6 → a pattern may go down; the rule is 'take away 6 each time', so the next number is smaller

point.hi: Yeh pattern hai 38, 32, 26, 20. Har chhalaang peeche ki taraf hai, aur har baar 6 ghatta hai. Pattern ghat bhi sakta hai. Iska niyam hai: har baar 6 ghatao.
point.en: This pattern is 38, 32, 26, 20. Every jump goes backwards, and it goes down by 6 each time. A pattern can go down too. Its rule is: take away 6 each time.

prompt.hi: Board ke pattern 38, 32, 26, 20 mein 20 ke baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: In the board's pattern 38, 32, 26, 20, which number comes after 20?

explain.convey: 2, 4, 8, 16: steps 2, 4, 8 are not equal, but each number is double the one before → rule 'double each time'

point.hi: Is pattern 2, 4, 8, 16 mein chhalaang barabar nahi: pehle 2, phir 4, phir 8. Par 2 ka dugna 4 hai, 4 ka dugna 8, aur 8 ka dugna 16. Toh niyam hai: har baar dugna karo.
point.en: In this pattern 2, 4, 8, 16 the jumps are not equal: first 2, then 4, then 8. But double 2 is 4, double 4 is 8, and double 8 is 16. So the rule is: double each time.

prompt.hi: Board ke pattern 2, 4, 8, 16 mein 16 ke baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: In the board's pattern 2, 4, 8, 16, which number comes after 16?

explain.convey: 1, 3, 6, 10: steps 2, 3, 4 → the step itself grows by 1 each time; a changing step can be a regular rule too

point.hi: Ab 1, 3, 6, 10 dekho. Kadam hain 2, phir 3, phir 4. Yahan kadam khud har baar 1 badhta hai. Yeh bhi ek niyam hai.
point.en: Now look at 1, 3, 6, 10. The steps are 2, then 3, then 4. Here the step itself grows by 1 each time. That is a rule too.

prompt.hi: Board ke pattern 1, 3, 6, 10 mein 10 ke baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: In the board's pattern 1, 3, 6, 10, which number comes after 10?

problem.hi: Pattern hai 96, 48, 24, 12. Iska agla number kaunsa hai?
problem.en: The pattern is 96, 48, 24, 12. What is its next number?

do.hi: Har kadam pe kitna ghata, yeh nikalo
do.en: Find how much goes down at each step

why.hi: 96 se 48, 48 se 24, aur 24 se 12 alag-alag ghate
why.en: 96 to 48, 48 to 24 and 24 to 12 went down by different amounts

do.hi: Ab har number ko pichhle number se milao
do.en: Now compare each number with the one before

steps.result: har number pichhle ka aadha hai

why.hi: 96 ka aadha 48, 48 ka aadha 24, aur 24 ka aadha 12 hai
why.en: half of 96 is 48, half of 48 is 24, and half of 24 is 12

prompt.hi: Niyam mil gaya: har baar aadha karo. Toh 12 ke baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: We have the rule: take half each time. So which number comes after 12?

why.hi: har number pichhle ka aadha hai, aur 12 ka aadha 6 hai
why.en: each number is half the one before, and half of 12 is 6

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 50, 44, 38, 32. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 50, 44, 38, 32. Which number comes after it?

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 4, 8, 16, 32. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 4, 8, 16, 32. Which number comes after it?

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 4, 7, 11, 16, 22. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 4, 7, 11, 16, 22. Which number comes after it?

ladder.why: falling game points 94, 86, 78 → −8 checked on both steps
predict 27 or 48 for 3, 6, 12, 24 → steps unequal, the rule is double
harder: the amount taken away grows 3, 6, 9, 12 → next takes away 15

remediation.move: number line with backward jumps: read each jump aloud as minus 5; ask which way the jumps go before choosing the next number

say.hi: 60, 55, 50, 45 mein har chhalaang peeche ki taraf hai, har baar 5 kam. Numbers chhote hote ja rahe hain, toh agla number bhi chhota hi hoga.
say.en: In 60, 55, 50, 45 every jump goes backwards, 5 less each time. The numbers keep getting smaller, so the next number will be smaller too.

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 70, 63, 56, 49. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 70, 63, 56, 49. Which number comes after it?

remediation.move: difference row: write every gap under 1, 3, 7, 13 → 2, 4, 6; gaps not equal but grow by 2 → never predict from the first gap alone

say.hi: Har do numbers ke beech ka farak likho. 1, 3, 7, 13 mein farak hain 2, 4 aur 6. Farak barabar nahi, par har baar 2 badhta hai, isliye sirf pehla farak dekh ke aage mat badho.
say.en: Write the gap between every two numbers. In 1, 3, 7, 13 the gaps are 2, 4 and 6. The gaps are not equal, but they grow by 2 each time, so do not go on from the first gap alone.

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 5, 6, 8, 11, 15. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 5, 6, 8, 11, 15. Which number comes after it?

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab pattern ka niyam dhoondhna aa gaya. Ab niyam ko shabdon mein bolenge, aur calendar aur shapes ke pattern mein use karenge.
bridgeToNext.en: Now we can find a pattern's rule. Next we will say the rule in words and use it in calendar and shape patterns.

hook.convey: rules in words live in real things: practice every Saturday → calendar dates a week apart; squares drawn in a row share a side → a fixed number of new lines per square

use.hi: Tumhari cricket practice har Saturday hoti hai, aur is mahine pehli practice 6 tareekh ko hai. Baaki practice kis tareekh ko hongi, yeh calendar ka pattern batayega.
use.en: Your cricket practice is every Saturday, and this month the first practice is on the 6th. On which dates are the other practices? The calendar's pattern will tell.

use.hi: Drawing book mein seedhi lines se squares ki ek line draw karo. Har naya square pichhle square se ek line share karta hai. Kitni lines lagengi, iska bhi ek niyam hai.
use.en: In your drawing book, draw a row of squares with straight lines. Each new square shares one line with the square before. How many lines it takes also has a rule.

explain.convey: matchstick squares in a row: 1 square 4 sticks, 2 squares 7, 3 squares 10 → each new square shares a stick and needs 3 more; rule in words 'start at 4, add 3 for each new square' finds a later count

point.hi: Maachis ki teeliyon se jude squares dekho. 1 square ke liye 4 teeli lagti hain. Agla square pichhle se ek teeli share karta hai, isliye 2 square ke liye 7 teeli, aur 3 square ke liye 10. Niyam shabdon mein: 4 se shuru karo, har naye square pe 3 teeli jodo.
point.en: Look at joined squares made of matchsticks. 1 square takes 4 sticks. The next square shares one stick with the one before, so 2 squares take 7, and 3 squares take 10. The rule in words: start at 4, add 3 sticks for each new square.

prompt.hi: Board ki tarah line mein 5 jude squares banane hain. Kitni teeliyan lagengi?
prompt.en: We want to make 5 joined squares in a row, like on the board. How many sticks will it take?

explain.convey: calendar column = the same weekday; one row down = one week later = +7 (not +1); Mondays 4, 11, 18, 25

point.hi: Calendar ke ek column mein ek hi din hota hai, jaise saare Monday. Ek Monday se agla Monday poore ek hafte baad aata hai, aur hafte mein 7 din hote hain. Isliye column mein neeche jaane par har baar 7 judta hai: 4, 11, 18, 25.
point.en: One calendar column holds the same day, like all the Mondays. One Monday comes a whole week after the last, and a week has 7 days. So going down a column adds 7 each time: 4, 11, 18, 25.

prompt.hi: Is mahine 11 tareekh Monday hai, aur uske theek neeche 18. Toh 12 tareekh, Tuesday, ke theek neeche kaunsi tareekh hogi?
prompt.en: This month the 11th is a Monday, and just below it is the 18th. So which date is just below the 12th, a Tuesday?

problem.hi: Ek mahine mein 31 din hain, aur 2 tareekh ko Tuesday hai. Us mahine ke saare Tuesday ki tareekhein batao.
problem.en: A month has 31 days, and the 2nd is a Tuesday. Give the dates of all the Tuesdays in that month.

find.hi: mahine ke saare Tuesday ki tareekhein
find.en: the dates of all the Tuesdays in the month

do.hi: Pehle niyam banao: agla Tuesday ek hafte baad aata hai
do.en: First make the rule: the next Tuesday comes one week later

prompt.hi: 23 tareekh ke baad agla Tuesday kis tareekh ko aayega?
prompt.en: After the 23rd, on what date does the next Tuesday come?

why.hi: har Tuesday pichhle se 7 din baad aata hai, aur 30 + 7 = 37 mahine ke 31 din se aage hai
why.en: each Tuesday comes 7 days after the last, and 30 + 7 = 37 is past the month's 31 days

prompt.hi: Calendar pe 8 tareekh Friday hai. Uske theek neeche, agla Friday kis tareekh ko hoga?
prompt.en: On a calendar the 8th is a Friday. Just below it, on what date is the next Friday?

prompt.hi: {friend} ka birthday 14 tareekh, Sunday ko hai. Usse ek hafta pehle wala Sunday kis tareekh ko tha?
prompt.en: {friend}'s birthday is on the 14th, a Sunday. On what date was the Sunday one week before it?

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 6, 12, 24. {friend} ka kehna hai ki iska niyam 'har baar 6 jodo' hai. Kya yeh niyam teeno numbers pe sahi hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The pattern is 6, 12, 24. {friend} says its rule is 'add 6 each time'. Does this rule work for all three numbers, yes or no?

accept: nahi, har baar dugna hota hai

ladder.why: calendar column 3, 10, 17 → down a column adds 7
error spot: next Monday below the 5th is not the 6th → +7, the 12th
shape pattern: joined matchstick triangles → say the rule 'add 2', then 4 triangles
rule in words on savings: ₹5 more each day → carry it to day 6
harder: tile stages 5, 8, 11 → use the rule four stages ahead to stage 7

remediation.move: a month calendar with one column lit: each row is one whole week → the date below is 7 days later, never the next day

say.hi: Calendar ki har line ek poora hafta hai, yaani 7 din. Isliye kisi tareekh ke theek neeche wali tareekh 7 din baad aati hai, jaise 9 ke neeche 16.
say.en: Each row of the calendar is a whole week, that is 7 days. So the date just below any date comes 7 days later, like 16 below 9.

prompt.hi: Calendar pe 20 tareekh Thursday hai. Uske theek neeche wali tareekh kaunsi hai?
prompt.en: On a calendar the 20th is a Thursday. Which date is just below it?

remediation.move: test the rule on every step, not only the first: 6 → 12 is +6 but 12 → 24 is +12; each number is double the one before → a doubling list, then a fresh doubling list to continue

say.hi: Niyam ko har kadam pe check karo. 6 se 12 tak 6 juda, par 12 se 24 tak 12 juda. Har number pichhle ka dugna hai, toh niyam 'har baar 6 jodo' nahi hai.
say.en: Check the rule on every step. From 6 to 12, 6 was added, but from 12 to 24, 12 was added. Each number is double the one before, so the rule is not 'add 6 each time'.

prompt.hi: Pattern hai 5, 10, 20, 40. Iske baad kaunsa number aayega?
prompt.en: The pattern is 5, 10, 20, 40. Which number comes after it?
